newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Lippo sweetens acquisition plans.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Lippo sweetens acquisition plans.

text.p: Indonesia's Lippo group said on Thursday it will sweeten terms to restructure its financial services group through a six-point plan.
"Lippo today announced substantially sweetened terms for the financial restructuring of Lippo's financial services group," the group said in a statement.
It said it will permanently waive the 10 percent management fee on Lippo bank's pre-tax earnings, effective from September 30, 1996.
"This waiver is worth at least 680 billion rupiah, assuming a conservative 15 percent earnings growth rate and a 17 percent discount rate," it said.

Lippo announced a massive internal acquisition plan early this month to restructure its financial services. Under the plan, Lippo Securities will buy an additional 27 percent share of Lippo Life to increase its stake to 32 percent.
Lippo Life will then buy another 40 percent share of Lippo Bank to boost its stake to 45 percent.
Lippo said another voluntary waiver would reduce the acquisition price of Lippo Life by Lippo Securities to 237 billion rupiah from 244 billion rupiah.
It said an additional waiver would reduce the purchase price of Lippo Bank by Lippo Life to 638 billion rupiah from 658 billion rupiah initially.

Lippo, one of the country's largest conglomerates, said Lippo Securities will announce its intention to proceed with a rights issue of between 500 billion rupiah to one trillion rupiah within 12 months.
Lippo said its insurance arm Lippo Life also planned to conduct a rights issue of between 350 billion rupiah to 500 billion rupiah within 15 months.
Both rights issues will be subject to regulatory and shareholders' approvals.

It said the Riady family, controlling shareholder of Lippo Group, would make an official announcement that it will commit the proceeds of the notes under the financial restructuring to subscribe to the proposed rights issue at Lippo Securities and any rights that might become available under that plan.
Lippo said the family, Lippo Bank and Lippo Life would reduce the percentage of reserve cross-holdings in an orderly manner over an appropriate period of time.
James Riady, deputy chairman of Lippo Group, declined to give details on how the reduction of the reserve cross holdings would proceed. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
